newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's Pure seeks import duty waiver.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Pure seeks import duty waiver.

text.p: Pure Beverages Co Ltd, Sri Lanka's sole bottler of Coca Cola, has asked the government for a duty waiver to import the soft drink to meet a shortage from a two-month old strike, a company official said on Tuesday.
"We have sought a duty waiver. But so far we have not had a response from the government," said the official, who declined to be named.
The two Coca Cola bottling plants run by Pure Beverages have been closed since December 12 after some 700 workers walked out in a dispute over proposed lay-offs.
Pure Beverages is a 51 percent subsidiary of F&NCC, the regional bottler based in Singapore.

F&NCC, a joint venture of Coca Cola Co and Singapore's Fraser & Neave, bought the controlling stake in Pure Beverages for $13 million in November 1994. The Sri Lankan firm earlier operated as a Coca Cola franchise.
Coca Cola, Fanta and Sprite disappeared from shelves in Colombo and elsewhere in Sri Lanka, but the demand for soft drinks was being met by Pepsi and the local Elephant brand.
Coca Cola's daily output before the strike was 40,000 cases, the company official said.
"We would like to import Coke from a nearby market to at least partially fill the vacuum created locally by the strike," the company official said.
The government charges a 35 percent duty on imported soft drinks.
